subtopics.title: The Metric Ladder and the Marks in Units

questions.question: A household uses 18 kℓ of water in a month. In litres that is:
The direction rule for metric conversions is:
options: Converting to a SMALLER unit means more of them, so multiply; to a LARGER unit, divide
Multiply for mass, divide for length

questions.question: A room is given as 4,2 m by 340 cm. The correct first move is to:
options: Convert both to the same unit — 4,2 m by 3,4 m — before calculating

questions.question: An answer stating that a bath holds 8 000 litres should prompt you to:
options: Write it down and move on
Check the arithmetic — the estimate is far too large for the real world

subtopics.title: Crossing Into Imperial: Inches, Pounds and Miles

questions.question: A 50 kg pocket of cement, using 1 kg ≈ 2,2 pounds, weighs about:
A man six foot tall, using 1 foot = 30,48 cm, is:
A speed limit of 60 miles per hour, using 1 mile ≈ 1,609 km, is about:
The reliable way to decide whether to multiply or divide when crossing systems is:
options: Follow the order the units appear in the question
Ask which unit is BIGGER — the bigger unit converts into a larger NUMBER of the smaller one

questions.question: Converting 350 °F to Celsius gives:
options: 176,67 °C, so the oven is set to 180 °C

questions.question: A child's temperature of 38,5 °C in Fahrenheit is:
The duration from 14:20 to 16:05 is:
A bus leaves Mthatha at 05:45 and travels for six hours forty. It arrives at:

subtopics.title: Proportional Conversions: Coverage, Doses and Recipes

questions.question: Paint covering 20 m² per 5 ℓ is needed for a 54 m² wall given two coats. The volume required is:
With 5 ℓ tins at R429 and a 20 ℓ drum at R1 549, the cheaper way to reach 30 ℓ is:
options: One 20 ℓ drum plus two 5 ℓ tins at R2 407 — R167 cheaper

questions.question: A dose of 7,5 mℓ three times a day for five days needs:
options: 112,5 mℓ — so two 100 mℓ bottles must be bought

questions.question: Scaling a recipe for 4 up to 30 servings, the 3 eggs become:
options: 22,5 eggs, so 23 eggs are bought — quantities like eggs and paint round UP

questions.question: The number that the whole metric system is built on is:
options: One thousand — millimetres in a metre, metres in a kilometre, grams in a kilogram, millilitres in a litre

questions.question: The unit that breaks the thousand rhythm is:
options: The centimetre — there are a hundred in a metre

questions.question: Which everyday anchor is useful for estimating?
options: A brick is about a metre long
A teaspoon holds about a litre
A walking step is roughly a metre and a big cool drink bottle holds two litres
A bag of mealie meal weighs about a tonne

questions.question: When one measurement is in centimetres and another in metres, you should:
options: Convert both into the same unit FIRST, then calculate

questions.question: Coming DOWN from Fahrenheit to Celsius, the order of steps is:
options: Subtract 32 first, then multiply by 5, then divide by 9
Multiply by 9, divide by 5, then subtract 32

questions.question: The two temperature scales need a formula rather than a single multiplier because:
options: They do not start at the same place — water freezes at 0 °C but at 32 °F
Celsius is metric and metric always uses 1 000

questions.question: An imported bag labelled 33 pounds, at 2,2 pounds per kilogram, is:

subtopics.title: How Much Paint, How Much Medicine

questions.question: If 5 ℓ of paint covers 20 m², one litre covers:
A complete answer to "what should she buy?" is:
options: One 20 ℓ drum and two 5 ℓ tins, costing R2 407 — R167 cheaper than six tins
Six tins, because tins are easier to carry

questions.question: Scaling a recipe from 4 servings to 30 means multiplying every quantity by:
The rounding rule that fits the context is:
options: Round everything to the nearest whole number
Round everything down to be safe
Round only at the start of the calculation
Round paint and eggs UP, round money to cents, and never round a medicine dose
